extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/representatives, and patent office officials (receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, International Preliminary Examining Authorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory rules for drafting and filing an international (PCT) patent application: the Request, Description, Claims, Drawings, Abstract, priority claims, declarations, admissible content, and related procedural/transmittal requirements under the PCT Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and Languages of the Treaty instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: This Treaty shall be signed in a single original in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic; official texts in other languages shall be established by the Director General after consultation, and certified copies of the Treaty and Regulations and of any amendments shall be transmitted by the Director General to Contracting States and, on request, other States; the Director General shall register the Treaty with the UN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 67–68 set the formal depositary and transmission functions: two certified copies transmitted; registration with United Nations; certified copies of amendments transmitted; languages designated by Assembly; Treaty open for signature until specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications by the Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall notify Governments of all States party to the Paris Convention of: signatures, deposits of instruments of ratification/accession, date of entry into force and date from which Chapter II is applicable, declarations under Article 64(1)–(5), withdrawals of certain declarations, denunciations under Article 66, and declarations under Article 31(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 69 enumerates the specific items to be notified to Contracting States for transparency and procedural effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Treaty', 'Chapter' and 'Article' (abbreviated expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In these Regulations, the word 'Treaty' means the Patent Cooperation Treaty; the words 'Chapter' and 'Article' refer to the specified Chapter or Article of the Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 1 provides definitions of abbreviated expressions to ensure consistent interpretation across the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Applicant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the word 'applicant' is used, it shall be construed as meaning also the agent or other representative of the applicant, except where the contrary clearly follows from the wording or nature of the provision or context (e.g., where provision refers to residence or nationality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.1 clarifies that 'applicant' can include representatives for purposes of the Regulations unless context requires otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Agent'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the word 'agent' is used, it shall be construed as meaning an agent appointed under Rule 90.1, unless the contrary clearly follows from the wording, nature of the provision, or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.2 ties the term 'agent' to appointment under the Administrative Instructions (Rule 90.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Common Representative'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the expression 'common representative' is used, it shall be construed as meaning an applicant appointed as, or considered to be, the common representative under Rule 90.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.2 bis clarifies who qualifies as a common representative for multi-applicant filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Signature' (and seal equivalence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the word 'signature' is used, it shall be understood that, if the national law applied by the receiving Office or the competent ISA/IPEA requires a seal instead of a signature, the word shall mean seal for that Office or Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.3 accommodates national formalities (signatures vs seals) to avoid formality rejections when national law differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Period definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'priority period' in relation to a priority claim means 12 months from the filing date of the earlier application whose priority is claimed; the day of filing of the earlier application is not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.4 sets the standard 12‑month Paris Convention priority period and cross-references Rule 80.5 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of the Request (Rule 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall be made on a printed form or be presented as a computer print-out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices must accept the printed form or computer print-out format for the Request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of printed forms (Rule 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the printed form shall be furnished free of charge to applicants by the receiving Office or, if the receiving Office desires, by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices must provide printed request forms free to applicants (or delegate that to the IB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check list contents on the Request (Rule 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall contain a list indicating: (i) total number of sheets constituting the international application and number of sheets of each element (request, description, claims, drawings, abstract, sequence listing part if any); (ii) where applicable, that the application is accompanied by a power of attorney, copy of general power, priority document, sequence listing in electronic form, payment document or other specified documents; (iii) number of the figure applicant suggests to accompany the abstract (applicant may suggest more than one figure in exceptional cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to complete the checklist, the receiving Office should make necessary indications except it shall not indicate the figure number for abstract; checklist particulars for printouts are prescribed by Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars of printed request and computer print‑out (Rule 3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars of the printed request form and of a request presented as a computer printout shall be prescribed by the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions supply the required specifics for request formatting and particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and optional contents of the Request; Signature (Rule 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall contain: (a) mandatory contents — a petition, the title of the invention, indications concerning the applicant and the agent, and indications concerning the inventor where required by national law; (b) where applicable — a priority claim, indications relating to an earlier search, a reference to a parent application or parent patent, an indication of applicant's choice of competent International Searching Authority; (c) may contain — certain other indications (e.g., inventor where not required, requests to transmit priority document, declarations under Rule 4.17, statement under Rule 4.18, request for restoration of priority); the Request shall be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 4.1 enumerates mandatory elements that must appear in the Request and lists optional/allowed items; signature by applicant(s) is required (see Rule 4.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention — brevity and precision (Rule 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention shall be short (preferably from two to seven words when in English or translated into English) and precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles should be concise for clarity and standardized publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and addresses format (Rule 4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of natural persons indicated by family name before given name(s); legal entities by full official designations; addresses must satisfy customary requirements for prompt postal delivery (include all administrative units up to house number where applicable); recommended to indicate teleprinter, telephone, fax or similar contact information; for each applicant, inventor or agent only one address may be indicated except an additional address for notifications may be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper formatting of names/addresses facilitates communication and avoids delays; failure to include house number has no effect where national law does not require it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identification requirements (Rule 4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall indicate the name, the address, and the nationality and residence of the applicant, or of each applicant if several; nationality indicated by State of which the person is a national; residence indicated by State of which the person is a resident; Request may indicate different applicants for different designated States; where applicant is registered with national Office acting as receiving Office, Request may indicate registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete applicant identification is mandatory to meet formal requirements and for national processing differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor identification requirements (Rule 4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the Request shall indicate the name and address of the inventor(s); if applicant is the inventor, a statement to that effect may be used in lieu of separate inventor indication; Request may indicate different persons as inventors for different designated States where national laws differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor indications must follow national requirements and may vary by designated State; include name/address when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent identification (Rule 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent is appointed, the Request shall indicate and state the agent's name and address; where the agent is registered with the national Office acting as receiving Office, the Request may indicate the registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent identification enables official communications and is mandatory when an agent represents the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative indication (Rule 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a common representative is appointed, the Request shall so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring a common representative is required where one is appointed to act for multiple applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of States and kinds of protection (Rule 4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing the Request constitutes (i) the designation of all Contracting States bound by the Treaty on the international filing date; (ii) an indication that the international application is for the grant of every kind of protection available in each designated State to which Articles 43 or 44 applies; (iii) an indication for States to which Article 45(1) applies that the application is for the grant of a regional patent and, unless Article 45(2) applies, also a national patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 4.9 clarifies the legal effects of filing a PCT Request as to designation and types of protection sought at the national/regional level, with special transitional provisions for certain national laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim content and form (Rule 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any priority claim must be made in the Request and consist of a statement that priority of an earlier application is claimed and must indicate: (i) date of earlier filing; (ii) number of earlier application; (iii) where earlier application is national — the country in which it was filed; (iv) where earlier application is regional — the authority entrusted with granting regional patents; (v) where earlier application is an international application — the receiving Office with which it was filed. Additional indications for regional/international earlier applications may be given (e.g., countries for which the earlier application was filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 4.10 sets the mandatory bibliographic data for valid priority claims and options for specifying member Countries/authorities to meet Paris Convention/PRIORITY requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to continuation/continuation‑in‑part or parent application/grant (Rule 4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant intends that the international application be treated as a patent of addition, continuation, or continuation-in-part, the Request must indicate this and identify the relevant parent application, parent patent, or other parent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including such an indication has no effect on designation operations under Rule 4.9 but is required to trigger specific national procedural treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of earlier search (Rule 4.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes the ISA to take into account results of an earlier international, international-type or national search, the Request shall so indicate and specify the Authority/Office and the application concerned; the Request may, where applicable, state that the international application is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application, or the same except for language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing earlier search details enables the ISA to consider prior work and possibly avoid duplication; specification of the earlier search source is mandatory to invoke this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of International Searching Authority (Rule 4.14 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more International Searching Authorities are competent for the international application, the applicant shall indicate his choice of International Searching Authority in the Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where more than one ISA is competent, the applicant must select which ISA will perform the international search; competence rules are elsewhere in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature of the Request (Rule 4.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall be signed by the applicant or, if there is more than one applicant, by all of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal signature requirement: unsatisfied signature may cause formality defects or require correction per Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transliteration or translation of names/addresses (Rule 4.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any name or address is written in non-Latin characters, the same shall also be indicated in Latin characters either as a transliteration or through translation into English; the applicant decides which words are transliterated vs translated. The name of any country in non-Latin characters shall also be indicated in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure consistent identification in international processing and publication; applicant discretion on transliteration vs translation subject to rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations for national requirements (Rule 4.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request may, for national law purposes in designated States, contain one or more declarations worded as prescribed by Administrative Instructions, including (i) identity of the inventor, (ii) applicant’s entitlement as at the international filing date to apply for and be granted a patent, (iii) applicant’s entitlement to claim priority, (iv) declaration of inventorship as in Rule 51 bis.1(a)(iv) (signed per Admin Instr.), and (v) declaration as to non‑prejudicial disclosures or exceptions to lack of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These declarations are optional in the Request but when provided must follow the prescribed wording in Administrative Instructions to satisfy national requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of incorporation by reference (Rule 4.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application claims priority and an element or part of the application is completely contained in the earlier application but not otherwise contained in the international application, the Request may contain a statement that that element or part is incorporated by reference in the international application for purposes of Rule 20.6, subject to confirmation under Rule 20.6; such a statement, if not in the Request on the filing date, may be added only if it was otherwise contained in or submitted with the international application on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference is narrowly permitted and subject to confirmation procedures to ensure the material is in fact present in the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional matter in the Request (Rule 4.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall contain no matter other than that specified in Rules 4.1 to 4.18; Administrative Instructions may permit but cannot make mandatory inclusion of additional matter specified therein. If additional matter is present, the receiving Office shall ex officio delete it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Request is strictly limited to prescribed content; extraneous material will be removed by the receiving Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of the Description (Rule 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall first state the title as in the Request and shall: (i) specify the technical field; (ii) indicate the background art useful for understanding/searching/examining the invention and preferably cite documents reflecting such art; (iii) disclose the invention, as claimed, in terms that the technical problem and its solution can be understood and state advantageous effects with reference to background art; (iv) briefly describe figures in the drawings; (v) set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention, in terms of examples where appropriate with reference to drawings (unless national law of designated State does not require best mode); (vi) explicitly indicate how the invention is capable of industrial exploitation and how it can be made and used (industry in broadest sense). The manner and order should be followed except when a different order results in better understanding; each part should preferably be preceded by an appropriate heading as suggested in Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5.1 provides the structure and minimum content for a description to meet sufficiency / disclosure expectations across national Offices; best mode requirement is subject to national law variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosure (Rule 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences required to be included in a sequence listing pursuant to Administrative Instructions, the description shall include a sequence listing part complying with the standard provided in the Administrative Instructions; language‑dependent free text in the sequence listing need not be included in the main description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must follow Administrative Instructions standards and can be contained in a distinct sequence-listing part of the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and numbering of claims (Rule 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of claims shall be reasonable in consideration of the nature of the invention; if multiple claims, they shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals. Method of numbering for amended claims governed by Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive claim counts; follow conventional consecutive Arabic numeral numbering; amended-claim numbering rules may be specified administratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to other parts of the application in claims (Rule 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not, except where absolutely necessary, rely in respect of technical features on references to the description or drawings (e.g., 'as described in part ...' or 'as illustrated in figure ...'); where drawings exist, technical features in claims should preferably be followed by reference signs placed between parentheses, which may be removed by designated Offices for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be self-contained and define technical features in claim language rather than by cross-reference; use reference signs only to facilitate understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of claiming (two‑part/form/characterizing portion) (Rule 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter for which protection is sought shall be defined in terms of technical features. Whenever appropriate, claims shall contain: (i) a statement indicating those technical features which are necessary for the definition but which, in combination, are part of the prior art; and (ii) a characterizing portion—preceded by words such as 'characterized in that', 'characterized by', 'wherein the improvement comprises', or similar—stating concisely the technical features which, in combination with the features under (i), it is desired to protect. Where national law does not require such manner, failure to use it has no effect if the claim used satisfies national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part claim form is preferred where appropriate (particularly for inventions building on prior art); wording for the characterizing portion should be concise and standardized to clarify the novel features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims format and grouping (Rule 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim includes all features of one or more other claims and shall do so by a reference (preferably at the beginning) to the other claim(s) and then state additional features. A multiple dependent claim referring to more than one other claim shall refer to such claims in the alternative only; multiple dependent claims shall not serve as basis for another multiple dependent claim. Dependent claims shall be construed as including all limitations of the claim to which they refer. All dependent claims referring back to a single previous claim and those referring back to several previous claims shall be grouped together to the extent practical. If national law of the Office acting as ISA does not allow a different drafting of multiple dependent claims, failure to use the provided manner may result in an indication under Article 17(2)(b) in the international search report; failure to use the said manner has no effect in a designated State if the used manner satisfies that national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims must be properly referenced and grouped; multiple dependent claims have specific format constraints and may trigger an Article 17 indication if non‑conforming to the ISA's national practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model option (Rule 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated State in which a utility model is sought on the basis of an international application may, instead of Rules 6.1–6.4, apply the provisions of its national law concerning utility models once processing has started in that State, provided the applicant is allowed at least two months from expiration of the time limit under Article 22 to adapt the application to meet national utility model requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be required to adapt claims/format to national utility model law within a provided two‑month adaptation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: flow sheets and diagrams; time limit for filing drawings (Rules 7.1–7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings. The time limit referred to in Article 7(2)(ii) for filing drawings or additional drawings shall be reasonable and in no case shorter than two months from the date of the written invitation requiring the filing of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may include flow diagrams; Offices must allow at least two months after invitation to supply drawings, which is the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract contents and form (Rule 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall consist of: (i) a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, claims, and drawings indicating the technical field and drafted to allow clear understanding of the technical problem, gist of the solution, and principal uses; (ii) where applicable, the chemical formula which best characterizes the invention among formulas contained in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must summarize the invention clearly to allow quick technical assessment; include a representative chemical formula when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract concision and prohibition on merit statements (Rules 8.1(b)–(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be as concise as the disclosure permits (preferably 50 to 150 words if in English or translated into English). The abstract shall not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstracts short (50–150 words preferred) and factual—no promotional or speculative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs in abstract (Rule 8.1(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each main technical feature mentioned in the abstract and illustrated by a drawing shall be followed by a reference sign, placed between parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reference signs in the abstract to tie key mentioned features to drawing figures when helpful for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection for abstract (Rule 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant fails to indicate which figure should accompany the abstract, or if the ISA finds other figures would better characterize the invention, the ISA shall indicate which figure(s) should accompany the abstract for publication; if ISA finds none of the figures useful, it shall notify the International Bureau and the abstract will be published without any figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may select the most illustrative figure(s) for abstract publication; applicants' suggestions are considered but ISA may override.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle for drafting abstract (Rule 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be drafted so it can efficiently serve as a scanning tool for searching in the particular art, especially by assisting the scientist, engineer or researcher in deciding whether there is a need to consult the international application itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts are intended to enable quick assessment by technical specialists; draft them to highlight the technical problem, solution gist and principal uses to guide searchers.
